note.after_visit_summary:
Today we discussed your drinking habits and how they may affect your health and mood. You’ve been drinking more than planned most nights, and you had one blackout that worried you. Your depression is currently in remission while taking bupropion XL 150 mg every morning, and we want to keep it that way. Your AUDIT C score shows risky drinking, and your PHQ-9 score is low, indicating good mood control. Your blood pressure is slightly elevated at 138/88, and your pulse is 90. No tremors were seen, and you appear calm and thinking clearly.

We are checking your liver with a blood test (liver panel and GGT) today. If results are normal, we will start a medication called Naltric Zone at 50 mg once daily to help reduce alcohol cravings. I will call you with the lab results before you begin this medication.

For now, please limit alcohol to no more than one drink per day and aim for at least three alcohol-free days each week. You are also being referred to the Riverbend Recovery Center outpatient program, which offers evening group sessions twice a week that should fit your schedule.

Continue taking bupropion XL 150 mg every morning. If you feel shaky, sweaty, or anxious when cutting back on alcohol, call us right away. If your mood worsens or you have thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 immediately.

We will recheck your blood pressure at your next visit. Please return in four weeks on October 30th for follow-up.
